blocks.text: 67 סֵדֶר אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ. 67
uncertainties: The title may have metegs (e.g. סֵֽדֶר, אָבִֽינוּ, מַלְכֵּֽנוּ). The top of the title is cropped in band1, so I cannot confirm them.

blocks.text: On Sabbath אבינו מלכנו is not recited.
פותחים הארון.
uncertainties: Small Rashi-script letters. The reading is confident, but the yod/vav forms are small.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ חָטָאנוּ לְפָנֶיךָ׃
uncertainties: In most lines there is a small vertical stroke beside the tsere under כּ in מַלְכֵּנוּ, and in some lines under the ב of אָבִינוּ. It may be a meteg (מַלְכֵּֽנוּ / אָבִֽינוּ). It is not clear enough to confirm, so I left it out. The same uncertainty applies to every line below.
There may be a meteg in לְפָנֶיךָ (לְפָנֶֽיךָ). Unclear.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אָתָּה׃
uncertainties: There may be a meteg under the aleph of אָתָּה.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ עֲשֵׂה עִמָּנוּ לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ חַדֵּשׁ עָלֵינוּ שָׁנָה טוֹבָה׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ בַּטֵּל מֵעָלֵינוּ כָּל־גְּזֵרוֹת קָשׁוֹת׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ בַּטֵּל מַחְשְׁבוֹת שֹׂנְאֵינוּ׃
uncertainties: שֹׂנְאֵינוּ is defective (no vav). The dot over the shin could be both the sin dot and a holam. Plene שׂוֹנְאֵינוּ is not visible.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ הָפֵר עֲצַת אוֹיְבֵינוּ׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כַּלֵּה כָּל־צַר וּמַשְׂטִין מֵעָלֵינוּ׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כַּלֵּה דֶּבֶר וְחֶרֶב וְרָעָב וּשְׁבִי וּמַשְׁחִית מִבְּנֵי בְרִיתֶךָ׃
uncertainties: This petition wraps onto a second, indented line starting at מִבְּנֵי.

blocks.text: *) אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ מְנַע מַגֵּפָה מִנַּחֲלָתֶךָ׃
uncertainties: The *) is the footnote marker, printed to the right of the line.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ שְׁלַח רְפוּאָה שְׁלֵמָה לְחוֹלֵי עַמֶּךָ׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ הַחֲזִירֵנוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה לְפָנֶיךָ׃
uncertainties: The dagesh in the bet of בִּתְשׁוּבָה is faint.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ סְלַח וּמְחַל לְכָל־עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ׃
uncertainties: The first vav of עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ seems to carry a holam (עֲוֹ). There may also be a meteg.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ מְחֵה וְהַעֲבֵר פְּשָׁעֵינוּ מִנֶּגֶד עֵינֶיךָ׃
אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ קְרַע רוֹעַ גְּזַר דִּינֵנוּ׃
uncertainties: The source looks plene (רוֹעַ). Defective רֹעַ is not ruled out because the letters are close together.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ מְחוֹק בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים כָּל־שִׁטְרֵי חוֹבוֹתֵינוּ׃
uncertainties: The type is set tightly, and מַלְכֵּנוּ and מְחוֹק almost touch. I take them as separate words.
מְחוֹק is plene in the source. I kept it as printed (the usual spelling is מְחֹק).

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ זְכוֹר כִּי עָפָר אֲנָחְנוּ׃
uncertainties: There is an extra vertical mark under אֲנָחְנוּ. It may be a meteg (אֲנָֽחְנוּ), but I cannot confirm it.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ זָכְרֵנוּ בְּזִכְרוֹן טוֹב לְפָנֶיךָ׃
uncertainties: I read בְּזִכְרוֹן with a shva under the kaf. I cannot tell whether the kaf has a dagesh.

blocks.text: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כָּתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר חַיִּים טוֹבִים׃

*) אין פֿירטה אונד איינִיגען געמיינדען ווערדען פֿאָן היער אָן דיא אבינו מלכנו אין פֿאָלגענדער אָרדנונג געבעטעט: אבינו מלכנו מנע מגפה. א"מ החזירנו. סלח ומחל. מחה והעבר. מחוק ברחמיך. קרע רוע. שלח רפואה. זכור כי. זכרנו. כתבנו בספר חיים. זכיות. פרנסה. מחילה וסליחה. גאולה וישועה. הצמח לנו וכו׳.
uncertainties: This is Judeo-German in Rashi script. In Rashi script, aleph looks like ח, so I transcribed the intended letters: אין, אונד, איינִיגען. Each word looks literally like חין, חונד, חייניגען.
Every אבינו/מלכנו in the footnote looks literally like אביט/מלכט in Rashi script (נו is ligature-like). I transcribed them as אבינו/מלכנו.
There is a rafe or diacritic over the pe in פֿאָן and פֿאָלגענדער, and qamatz-like marks under the alephs in אָן and אָרדנונג. The exact pointing is unclear.
The place name looks like פירטה (Fürth). It may have a rafe.
The word before פרנסה reads וכיות in the Rashi glyphs. I take it as זכיות.
The last item reads 'הצמח לנו' plus an abbreviation that looks like ח״ו or א״ו. I take it as וכו׳ (etc.), but this is uncertain.

blocks.text: 67 Abinu Malkenu 67
On Sabbath אבינו מלכנו is not recited.
The Holy Ark is opened.
אבינו
Our Father, our King, we have sinned before Thee.
Our Father, our King, we have no king but Thee.
Our Father, our King, deal with us kindly for the sake of Thy Name.
Our Father, our King, renew for us a good year.
Our Father, our King, annul all harsh decrees from upon us.
Our Father, our King, annul the plans of those that hate us.
Our Father, our King, frustrate the counsel of our enemies.
Our Father, our King, avert every foe and adversary from upon us.
Our Father, our King, avert pestilence, sword, famine, captivity and destruction from the children of Thy covenant.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates two words across line breaks: cap-tivity and chil-dren. I joined them.

blocks.text: Our Father, our King, hold back plague from Thine inheritance.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates inher-itance across a line break. I joined it.

blocks.text: Our Father, our King, send complete healing to the sick of Thy people.
Our Father, our King, restore us in complete repentance before Thee.
Our Father, our King, pardon and forgive all our sins.
Our Father, our King, blot out our transgressions and let them pass away from before Thine eyes.
Our Father, our King, tear up the severe verdict decreed against us.
Our Father, our King, erase in Thy great compassion all the records of our faults.
Our Father, our King, remember that we are dust.
Our Father, our King, remember us benevolently before Thee.
Our Father, our King, inscribe us in the book of good life.

notes: Both scans carry printed page number 67. s156 is the Hebrew page and s157 is the facing English translation.
The Hebrew Rashi-script rubric פותחים הארון. matches the English 'The Holy Ark is opened.'
The footnote on s156 has no English translation on s157, so I did not supply one.
Neither page has a biblical citation or attribution. Petition 17 (זכור כי עפר אנחנו) echoes Ps. 103:14, but the source does not cite it.

In several Hebrew lines there may be metegs beside the tsere of כּ in מַלְכֵּנוּ and the hiriq of ב in אָבִינוּ. They are not clear at this scan resolution, so I left them out and flagged them for review.
I used the bands only to check details and resolve seams. No lines are duplicated.
I propose no source typo corrections. Plene spellings such as מְחוֹק, זְכוֹר and רוֹעַ are kept as printed.
